Description: Whether to iteratively eliminate degree-1 and degree-2 buses and merge parallel lines. Runs once before and once after the target-count aggregation. Exact for the rest of the network (series combination is a Kron elimination), so switching it off costs bus count without buying fidelity.
Bus aggregation in ``simplify_network``: the caller names the cluster count and the distance references are calibrated from the network.
Whether to run the target-count aggregation at all. With this and ``low_degree_reduction`` both off the stage still converts voltage levels
column5: removes transformers and aggregates to substations.

Description: Number of clusters this pass produces. Not the bus count of the exported network -- the second low-degree reduction that follows shrinks it further. Must be at least the number of connected subgraphs left once region boundaries are cut.

Dimensionless weight on the electrical term. 1.0 weights effective reactance and geographic distance equally at the scale of a typical line; above 1 favours electrical proximity, below 1 favours geographic proximity.
Random probes used to approximate effective reactance and to calibrate the reference scales.

Probe columns kept as clustering features, setting how faithfully the effective-reactance term is reproduced: the relative error of the estimate is sqrt(2 / n_feature_dims). A subsample of the probes rather than a projection of them, so that error stays uniform across scales instead of concentrating on the short distances that decide the early merges.
Seed for the probe draw and subsample. Fixing it makes the busmap reproducible.
When building multiple networks, Use 'population' if you want to ensure the clusters are assigned constant names.
Implementation curerntly overrides to true. Network is simplified to substation nodes with positive or negative power injection.
Specifiy the method of aggregating fields within the generators, buses tables.
Specify the proportion of nodes to be attributed to a given zone in the form (California: 0.5) for half of all nodes to be located in California. Only used with TAMU Network
